expectedRealization.rationale: MSCI inclusion is structurally positive but implementation was about one year away, initial index weight only about 0.73%, and quality large caps were already strongly rerated before cutoff.

changeHypothesis.summary: MSCI formally approved A-share inclusion, improving structural international access, but actual index implementation was delayed to June 2018 with a small initial weight while high-quality large caps had already strongly outperformed.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: International ownership/access can improve structurally over years, but immediate passive flow at Q2 2017 cutoff was limited.
disconfirmingEvidence: Formal implementation was about one year away.
Initial pro-forma MSCI EM weight was only about 0.73%.
The frozen large-cap quality basket was already +19.50pp excess over 60d with 100% positive breadth.
Strong company fundamentals such as Midea's existed independently of MSCI and do not prove incremental MSCI earnings.

evidenceLedger.supportsClaim: MSCI inclusion is an official structural accessibility change, but delayed and initially small.
A representative quality large cap already had strong operating fundamentals independent of MSCI inclusion.
The quality large-cap basket had already rerated strongly before/around the announcement.

directWinners: A-shares eventually included in global indexes if foreign ownership demand grows
falseThemeMatches: any high-quality large cap treated as an immediate MSCI earnings beneficiary

selectionComparison.rationale: Company quality is not the same as an incremental MSCI event edge; delayed small initial flow plus strong prior rerating leaves no clean event-specific selection.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: The frozen quality large-cap basket was +8.81pp excess over 20d and +19.50pp over 60d with 100% positive 60d breadth.
expectations.thesisExpectation: Foreign ownership may structurally rise over years, but the 60-day base horizon does not have a large forced passive-flow catalyst.
expectations.measurableGap: No event-specific company earnings gap is measurable beyond already-recognized quality/large-cap rerating.

hypothesisDecompositionTest.productMarketScope: A-share large-cap accessibility/ownership under MSCI inclusion
hypothesisDecompositionTest.rationale: Keep structural ownership/accessibility separate from company operating earnings and from generic quality-factor performance.

nearTerm.driver: announcement effect versus no immediate inclusion flow

mediumTerm.driver: structural anticipation but formal inclusion still ~1 year away

evidenceHorizonMatrix.resolutionRule: Do not convert a long-duration ownership state into a base-horizon stock selection without a separate company/valuation edge.

leaderDivergenceTest.rationale: Quality companies are strong, but their operating strength predates and is not caused by the MSCI event.

valuationExecution.valuationContext: No selection on the MSCI event itself: structural accessibility is real, but immediate flow is delayed/small and quality large caps are already rerated.

bearCase: MSCI inclusion is genuinely positive long term but offers no special near/base-horizon edge beyond an already crowded quality/large-cap trade.

invalidationConditions.threshold: material near-term flow acceleration far above the frozen 0.73% initial-weight path

caveats: No post-cutoff selected-stock outcome is used before lock.

nextResearchActions: No event-specific selection; revisit only with a separate underabsorbed company/valuation edge or unexpectedly accelerated foreign flow.
